title: Add VPC control plane provisioning: subnets, endpoints, security groups, peering, and Route53 integrations
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds Terraform modules and defaults to provision VPC control plane resources for Redwood Private: auto-managed private subnets, interface endpoints for S3/SSM/EC2, control-plane security groups, optional cross-account VPC peering, and Route53 private hosted zone delegation. Opt-in by setting module variables; no automatic drift for existing control planes.
description:
Motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private need a repeatable, secure VPC pattern for control-plane components. This PR adds opinionated Terraform modules and examples to provision private subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, optional cross-account peering, and Route53 delegation so partners can deploy a fully-networked control plane without manual steps.

What this PR contains:
- A new module infra/terraform/modules/control-plane/vpc that creates private subnets (multi-AZ), NAT gateways (configurable), route tables, and associated tags.
- Interface endpoints (AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint) for S3, SSM, STS, EC2/ECR (configurable).
- Control-plane security groups tuned for least privilege and annotated with purpose.
- Optional cross-account VPC peering and IAM role assumptions to support multi-account private deployments with explicit allowlists.
- Route53 private hosted zone delegation and conditional Route53 resolver rules for cross-account DNS resolution.
- Examples and a workspace infra/terraform/examples/control-plane-vpc-aws with documented variables for most common deployment shapes.

Checklist: 
- [x] Terraform module implementing resources and outputs
- [x] Examples for single-account and cross-account peering
- [x] Integration tests (terraform plan/e2e smoke) run in CI
- [x] Updated docs snippet in redwood-docs/examples/private/vpc.md (links in PR)
- [x] Security review (Priya) and perf review (Daniel)

Backward compatibility and opt-in behavior: This change does not change defaults used by existing private installs. The example workspaces are opt-in; operators must adopt the new module and set variables to take control of their VPC resources. The module supports importing existing subnets/security groups where teams want to keep network ownership.

Testing and verification: I ran terraform fmt/validate, unit tests for helper scripts, and end-to-end plan/apply in a test account. CI performed a full plan and the e2e smoke applied resources in a sandbox VPC and validated DNS resolution across a peered account. See CI logs for plan output.

Migration notes: When migrating an existing private control plane to the managed module, operators should follow the migration guide in the examples folder. High-level: (1) create the module workspace with the exact VPC IDs/subnet IDs, (2) set import_existing_* flags, (3) ensure cross-account peering role trust is configured, (4) run terraform import for existing resources, (5) apply and verify.

Rollout plan: Merge to main, cut a minor release for redwood-private-installer referencing the new module, and ship documentation + a postman/terraform quickstart in redwood-quickstarts.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on the security group egress/ingress rules, the resolver-rule conditional logic, and IAM principal scoping for the peering role. The module attempts to follow least-privilege and annotates every resource with a redwood:managed tag.

TL;DR: Adds a production-ready Terraform module and examples to provision control-plane networking for Redwood Private with multi-account and DNS integration patterns.

notes_on_manual_steps: Operators must run terraform import for any existing VPC/subnet resources if migrating; see examples/migration.md for exact commands.
For cross-account peering, tenant must add the peering-role ARN to the trusted principals in the other account before apply to avoid race conditions.
DNS delegation requires updating Route53 resolver rules in the consumer account; the module emits outputs and a suggested Terraform snippet to manage resolver rules in the peered account.
environment_impacts: Creates interface endpoints which will consume VPC endpoint quotas in accounts.
Optional cross-account peering establishes routes; operators should review CIDR overlaps before enabling.
Route53 private hosted zone delegation modifies resolver rules and may affect intra-account DNS resolution temporarily during cutover.
